summary: array-flatten-utils ships a native-addon dropper that decrypts and executes a 6.7MB opaque payload on require()
details: The package presents itself as a lightweight array utility (flatten/compact/unique), but index.js unconditionally loads one of three platform-specific native addons at require time (native_win.node, native_mac.node, native.napi.node). The native loader references an adjacent encrypted blob shipped as.napi_cache (6,750,735 bytes, no extractable strings), stages a decoded executable to a temp path (/tmp/.<pid>), chmods it, and daemonizes it via fork+setsid+execlp. Before executing, the loader performs analysis-environment evasion: the Linux addon enumerates CI indicators (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NOW_GITHUB_DEPLOYMENT, CF_BUILD_ID, SCREWDRIVER) and container/debugger artifacts (/proc/1/cgroup, containerd, dockerinit, TracerPid in /proc/self/status, /proc/self/maps); the Windows addon imports CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, IsDebuggerPresent, CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, Process32First/Next, and SetFileAttributesA. The pure-JS array helpers are a cover story: a three-function utility has no legitimate reason to ship encrypted native blobs, drop them to /tmp, and spawn detached processes on import, let alone to gate that execution on sandbox/CI/debugger evasion. Importing array-flatten-utils executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
